paragraphs: The core of being a college nursing instructor is not finishing the textbook but turning nursing knowledge into safe care competence that students can execute, that can be observed, and that can be given feedback on; course objectives, cases, skill demonstrations, clinical preceptorship, and assessment must form a closed loop.

The value of the role comes from the dual traceability of competence and safety: one vague demonstration, one instance of letting unauthorized practice go unchecked, or one score without evidence can harm a student's development and amplify patient risk, so teaching progress cannot outrun supervision and authorization.

Positive signals are enjoying breaking down complex clinical judgment, patiently observing students' actions, giving specific feedback, and maintaining records; caution signals are liking only one-way lecturing, avoiding conflictual feedback, or being unwilling to keep updating nursing evidence and teaching methods.

Start with a 90-minute anonymized teaching exercise: choose one low-risk nursing concept and write a learning objective, a fictional case, a five-step demonstration, an observation scale, and feedback statements, without touching real patient or student data; then reflect on whether you enjoyed instructional design and evidence-based assessment.

This page uses U.S. O*NET 25-1072.00 as the precise occupational boundary: teaching and demonstrating patient care in classroom and clinical teaching units, where a post may emphasize teaching or combine teaching with research. Chinese rules are used separately to explain the boundaries of college teaching qualification and nurse practice.

entries: Analyze the curriculum and student learning needs and write assessable learning objectives.
Prepare handouts, cases, and laboratory or simulation teaching materials and organize classroom discussion.
Demonstrate nursing skills, supervise laboratory and clinical learning, and stop unauthorized or unsafe behavior promptly.
Assess assignments, examinations, skills, and clinical performance, and record grades, evidence, and feedback.
Update course content, take part in curriculum development and faculty collaboration, and possibly conduct research or service.

paragraphs: Work settings span classrooms, skills laboratories, simulation centers, and clinical teaching sites, and the pace is shaped by terms, timetabling, clinical rotations, and assessment milestones. Some posts also carry research, committee, or student advising duties, and the mix is decided by the institution and program.

Typical inputs are the curriculum plan, course standards, nursing evidence, student baseline, clinical site rules, and patient safety requirements; typical outputs are course materials, supervised practice, assessment records, feedback, improvement plans, and auditable teaching decisions.

Key judgments include whether objectives are observable, whether cases match current evidence, whether students can complete the task at the permitted level, whether performance differences come from knowledge or context, when to pause an activity and escalate, and whether grading is supported by consistent evidence.

A college nursing instructor is not the same as a clinical registered nurse, a general health professions teacher, or an ordinary college teacher. What they may share is communication and knowledge transfer; they differ in the learners taught, the depth of the nursing discipline, clinical supervision, patient safety responsibility, and practice authorization.

Evidence insufficient: the new-hire education composition percentages for O*NET 25-1072.00 were not obtained on the pages accessible this round (only the qualitative Job Zone 5 requirement was obtained). O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone 5, where most posts require graduate education and considerable experience; this describes the common U.S. preparation level, not a globally applicable license. Institutional appointment, teaching qualifications, nurse registration, and clinical site authorization must still be verified separately.

If you want to care for patients directly and carry out care plans on shifts, a clinical registered nurse is closer; if you want to design learning, observe skills, and assess students, a college nursing instructor is closer. The former centers on patient outcomes, the latter on student competence and patient safety as a dual center.

Health professions college teachers may teach public health, medical technology, or other health fields; a college nursing instructor must translate the nursing process, clinical judgment, skills, and professional standards into courses and clinical assessment, so the disciplinary boundary is narrower and deeper.

Ordinary college teachers also prepare lessons, teach, and assess, but nursing education often includes simulation or clinical sites, patient information, skill authorization, and high-consequence feedback. Whether a post involves real clinical preceptorship is a dividing line that must be verified when choosing a job.

If you most enjoy research design and publishing, compare posts that weight teaching and research together; if you most enjoy course delivery and student progress, compare teaching-focused posts; if you most enjoy the clinical site, compare clinical preceptorship or practice education posts.

Adjacent directions include college health professions teachers, ordinary college teachers, clinical registered nurses, middle and high school teachers, and clinical preceptorship and practice education directions; the comparison should distinguish them by learners taught, disciplinary depth, clinical supervision responsibility, and the authorization chain, not by similarity of job titles.

The adjacent links above come from batch routing and are for exploration, not proof of qualifications. Before choosing, read the recruitment notice directly to confirm the course level, clinical proportion, research requirements, teaching qualifications, nurse registration, professional title, and institutional appointment conditions.

Can assist: organizing confirmed course objectives into a draft syllabus and generating fictional case variants of different difficulty; the teacher must verify nursing evidence, difficulty, bias, and applicable population.
Can assist: drafting questions or scoring rubrics; it cannot directly decide item validity, fairness, the pass mark, or whether a student has reached clinical competence.

Can assist: categorizing anonymized feedback and common misconceptions; real student grades, identities, health information, or clinical records must not be entered into external models without approval.
Can assist: building search leads for public literature and policy; citations, currency, guideline versions, and clinical conclusions must be verified against the original authoritative sources.

Human control point: the teacher directly observes skills, clinical communication, and the judgment process and gives an assessment supported by scales and contextual evidence; model output is not a certificate of competence.

Human control point: when unauthorized practice, patient risk, privacy leakage, or conflicting evidence appears, pause, escalate, and record according to institutional and clinical site authorization; a chat tool must not handle it on its own.

Governance requirements: clarify authorized tools, data classification, human review, citation trails, error correction, and appeal routes; the model said so cannot become a basis for teaching or grading.

Editorial candidate change: lesson preparation, feedback, and material organization may explore tool assistance; this round did not obtain AI adoption rates, teaching effects, or causal net employment estimates for this occupation, so process restructuring is not written as a realized outcome.

This round did not obtain a precise national wage for Chinese college nursing instructors, which does not prove it has not been published. NBS2025 urban non-private education industry average 133,539 yuan/year is only industry background, not an occupational median.

For actual offers, verify region, appointment, establishment/contract, title, workload, research, and benefits.

Verify in writing the base salary, performance pay, teaching hours, preceptorship workload, research, social insurance, and promotion. Chinese college teaching qualifications, position appointment, and clinical nurse registration are verified separately. Articles 46—48 of the Higher Education Law concern qualification recognition, position conditions, and appointment contracts; Article 21 of the Measures for Implementing Teacher Qualification provides that provincial education administrative departments recognize qualifications and may lawfully entrust qualified institutions of higher education. Actually engaging in nursing activities requires a separate valid nurse registration and institutional authorization; teacher status does not exempt it.

U.S. O*NET 25-1072.00 had a median annual wage of 80,250 USD/year in 2025. The median is not a new-hire starting salary and does not represent an actual offer in a given state, institution, or contract type.

In the United States, the 10th percentile in 2025 was 48,800 USD and the 90th percentile was 129,500 USD; these are statistical positions in the national employee distribution and cannot be interpreted as a guaranteed range or a personal promotion path.

Institution type, region, degree level, teaching-research split, nine-month or year-round contract, clinical responsibilities, rank, and tenure track all affect pay. When comparing offers, the contract period and workload measures must be aligned.

The BLS overall postsecondary teachers page helps explain education paths and part-time patterns, but it is a combined occupational measure and cannot replace the precise O*NET wage for nursing instructors.

In the United States, specific qualifications are shaped jointly by state rules, program accreditation, institutional policy, and clinical site requirements; AACN's graduate-level nursing education and pedagogy recommendations are not a uniform statutory minimum for all posts.

Before accepting an offer, clarify base salary, summer teaching, clinical preceptorship compensation, research start-up, benefits, promotion criteria, and workload conversion. No national median can replace a written contract and a local cost-of-living check.

Fit is not a personality label. Use one micro-lesson, one rubric scoring, and one feedback rehearsal to test your preferences, then compare the purely clinical, teaching-focused, or combined teaching-research paths.

The risk controls below are editorial recommendations, not legal or AI governance requirements set by O*NET.
Main risks include insufficient clinical supervision, inconsistent grading, disclosure of student or patient privacy, AI citation errors, missing version records, and role overload.

O*NET tasks support teaching, supervision, assessment, and student record responsibilities; 75% considering accuracy extremely important and 78% working more than 40 hours per week are response shares and cannot be treated as incident rates, role overload rates, or a legal requirement for two-person calibration.
Teaching faculty, clinical preceptors, students, patients, and institutions may be affected; this round did not obtain comparative evidence on risk frequency across these groups.

Insufficient supervision can endanger patients, missing assessment evidence affects fairness and appeals, and records and erroneous citations affect traceability; the consequences are an editorial risk extrapolation, without incidence rates for the listed harms.

Actual positions may be called nursing lecturer, nursing teacher, clinical nursing instructor, simulation center instructor, or nursing teaching and research post; a job title does not mean the same teaching level, clinical responsibility, and research requirements, so read the duties and qualifications first.

paragraphs: Course completion, teacher training, software skills, or micro-credentials do not automatically grant college appointment, grade decision authority, clinical preceptorship, or nursing practice authority; authorization is decided jointly by the institution, the clinical site, the specific task, and local rules.

The competence ladder is based on output rather than years: first support course materials and skills laboratories under supervision, then independently deliver courses and assessment, and then expand to clinical preceptorship, course leadership, simulation education, program development, or teaching-research posts; each step requires corresponding qualifications, evidence, and authorization.

locale_requirements.credential_boundary: Teaching qualification, institutional appointment, professional title, nurse practice registration, and clinical site preceptorship authorization are mutually independent statuses, and none of them automatically confers clinical procedure or assessment authority beyond the authorized scope.
locale_requirements.jurisdiction: Chinese college teaching qualifications, position appointment, and clinical nurse registration are verified separately. Articles 46—48 of the Higher Education Law concern qualification recognition, position conditions, and appointment contracts; Article 21 of the Measures for Implementing Teacher Qualification provides that provincial education administrative departments recognize qualifications and may lawfully entrust qualified institutions of higher education. Actually engaging in nursing activities requires a separate valid nurse registration and institutional authorization; teacher status does not exempt it. In the United States, state clinical practice licensure and institutional/clinical site systems must also be verified.

personality_fit_block.boundary: The assessments are for exploration only; college teaching qualification, appointment, nurse registration, and clinical authorization are verified separately and cannot be replaced by a personality label or a paper portfolio.

questions.answer: Chinese college teaching qualifications, position appointment, and clinical nurse registration are verified separately. Articles 46—48 of the Higher Education Law concern qualification recognition, position conditions, and appointment contracts; Article 21 of the Measures for Implementing Teacher Qualification provides that provincial education administrative departments recognize qualifications and may lawfully entrust qualified institutions of higher education. Actually engaging in nursing activities requires a separate valid nurse registration and institutional authorization; teacher status does not exempt it.

questions.answer: Most posts require graduate-level preparation in nursing; specific appointment, program accreditation, and clinical preceptorship authorization are decided separately by the state, the institution, and the clinical site.

description.text: College nursing instructors (O*NET 25-1072.00) teach and demonstrate patient care in classrooms and clinical units and take on skill supervision, student assessment, and teaching improvement; this page explains occupational scope, tasks, China-U.S. qualification differences, and wage statistical measure boundaries based only on O*NET, BLS, AACN, the National Bureau of Statistics, and Chinese rules on college teaching qualification and nurse practice.

title.text: Nursing Instructors and Teachers, Postsecondary career profile｜teaching, qualifications, and boundaries

subject.name: College nursing instructors
subject.summary: College nursing instructors (O*NET-SOC 25-1072.00, Nursing Instructors and Teachers, Postsecondary) teach and demonstrate patient care to nursing students in classrooms and clinical teaching units, covering both teaching-focused faculty and posts that weight teaching and research together. This page uses the precise U.S. O*NET occupation as the scope boundary and uses Chinese rules to explain that college teaching qualification, institutional appointment, and nurse practice authorization are mutually independent qualifications.
